answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can forge trust from verifiable past work, not cheap identities: each agent carries a ledger of completed jobs, and a newcomer must anchor at a shared jetty — a checkpoint where sponsors stake reputation on its first tasks. A fake identity is free, but forging that history is not: an attacker must do auditable work or burn sponsor stake when fraud surfaces. As the tide of cheap identities rises, faking history costs more, because every new identity starts with zero earned trust and must pay its way in with checkable work.
